meta.title: HSK 3.0 Level 3 — English to Chinese
meta.subtitle: 491 words · recall the characters and pinyin
meta.desc: Shown an English meaning, recall the simplified form, the traditional form and the pinyin. The official HSK 3.0 Level 3 vocabulary as the standard now stands — the list announced at the end of 2025 and in force from 2026, not the 2021 list it replaced, which is a different and much longer one (500 words at Level 1 against 300). The official list has 500 rows, taking the cumulative total through this level to 1000. Every card carries the simplified form, the traditional form, the syllabus's own pinyin, bopomofo, the measure word where the word takes one, and the syllabus's own definition with its part of speech — the sense the exam means, rather than every sense the word has. Traditional characters are shown at half strength, and are omitted entirely where they are identical to the simplified — 225 of the 491 words. This deck has 491 cards rather than 500 because the syllabus lists a word again wherever it introduces a new sense, and a Folio card shows every sense a word has: 9 of this level's rows are words already carded in the Level 1 or Level 2 deck. Where the syllabus lists a word twice at the SAME level it has two readings to learn, and it gets one card showing both, with the definitions grouped under the reading they belong to. Each card also breaks the word into its characters, giving each one's reading, its meaning and the radical it is filed under, and carries a fold of three real example sentences, chosen to put the word in three different sentence shapes rather than the same one three times, with the word picked out in colour in each. Word list, pinyin and definitions: the official HSK 3.0 vocabulary lists. Traditional forms, bopomofo and measure words: CC-CEDICT (CC BY-SA 4.0). Radicals and character meanings: Make Me a Hanzi. Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
